newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices firm on fresh demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices firm on fresh demand.

text.p: Fresh demand pulled the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices up on Thursday amid tight supplies during the upcoming summer season, traders said.
Two 180-cst cargoes were heard traded both at $103.00 per tonne for June 1-4 and June 10-14 lifting respectively.
The 180-cst grade was bid at $102.00 per tonne on Wednesday and traded at $101.00 on Tuesday.
Little interest was seen in the SIMEX futures contract, with no transations reported late on Thursday.
The fuel oil swaps market was also quiet, with June unchanged at $101.50/$102.50 and July at $99.50/$101.00 against $99.75/$100.75.

Traders said over one million tonnes of fuel oil committed to a local trader arrived in Singapore since last week and the market has been widely speculating that the local trader would bid up the market.
The trader bought one cargo at $102.00 per tonne last week.
"But the trader has not been in the market so far this week," said one trader. "I doubt if they really want to bid up the market."
Traders said supplies will soon start tightening because of fewer exports from the Middle East during the summer season.
Maintenance turnarounds at South Korean refineries in May and June also boosted sentiment, they said.
But Singapore weekly residues stocks rose by 1.38 million barrels to 11.302 million barrels for the week ending May 14, Singapore's Trade Development Board (TDB) said on Thursday.
Some traders were skeptical over the recent gains.
"Supplies are tightening but there is no especially huge demand, so the rise should be limited," said one trader.
Taiwna's Chinese Petroleum Corp is expected to announce on Friday results of its tender to sell 30,000 tonnes of 3.0-percent sulphur fuel oil for June lifting.
In the LSWR market, an offer was heard at $15.20 but there was no buyer, traders said.
Sentiment has been bearish over ample supplies and traders said there are no signs for demand from Japan, the main LSWR importer.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
